separation_contract: Episode is immutable observed attempt evidence; diagnosis interprets the observed residual; failure scopes the failed method; obstruction states the remaining relation; lesson/motif are candidate abstractions only.

diagnosis.statement: The specialized Section-4 conservation-law consumer requires an asymptotic cutoff condition whose a-exponent is strictly positive throughout the producer-compatible Section-4 exponent polytope when F(a)=1; the producer/consumer regimes therefore do not overlap for condition (4.4).

failure.method_family: reuse Section-4 axial cutoff condition (4.4) and resulting conservation law to close the general F=1 ancient-Euler branch
failure.failure_mode: Under 3/s1+2/l1=4 and l1<=s1, l1<=5/4; therefore beta=2-(3/2)l1>=1/8. With F(a)=1 the (4.4) quantity is a^beta and cannot tend to zero.
competing_diagnoses_rejected: endpoint equality rescue: rejected because beta>=1/8 strictly
negative beta rescue: would require l1>4/3, contradicting l1<=5/4
silently change F(a): rejected because target fibre freezes F(a)=1

obstruction.relation: A specialized positive Euler conservation-law consumer may be valid in its own source family yet be unusable for a target producer when its asymptotic precondition is incompatible with the producer's scaling/exponent region.
obstruction.target_residual: The general F=1 branch still needs a source-inherited annular tightness, signed flux/telescoping, recentering/minimality, or another exact-compatible Euler rigidity interface.

expected_effects: avoid importing special-case rigidity into a nonoverlapping producer regime
keep local versus gluing residuals typed separately

candidate_lesson.falsifier: Find an admissible Section-4 pair satisfying the exact exponent constraints and F(a)=1 for which the printed (4.4) quantity tends to zero.

candidate_motif.statement: Before transporting a positive rigidity/conservation consumer across source families, substitute the target producer's exact scaling law into the consumer's asymptotic preconditions and solve the resulting feasible region.
